governanceNotes: D1 batch 61 (2026-09-26): one bounded association edge authored - morton-s-neuroma to metatarsalgia (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The proposition rests on the metatarsalgia differential-diagnosis review naming Morton's neuroma a main cause of lesser metatarsalgia (PMID 37230133), the anatomy-pathomechanism imaging review (PMID 33168237), and the 138-patient prospective outcomes study (PMID 33019802).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) constitutive proximity - the edge is deliberately scoped to the clinical syndrome framing (Morton's neuroma as a named cause of lesser metatarsalgia) rather than the identity's own defining forefoot pain; (ii) diagnostic mimic - intermetatarsal bursitis is documented to present identically with positive Mulder test and is excluded only by ultrasound (PMID 40677501); (iii) evidence class - review-level causation framing plus one observational outcomes study without incidence denominators; (iv) sibling-window discipline - the hallux-valgus and mallet-toes metatarsalgia windows keep their own evidence and none is recycled (ME-29); (v) withheld psychiatric and chronic-pain propositions - the semantic-mismatch guard blocks an unexplained-chronic-pain edge and no mood quantification was located.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Morton's neuroma documents lesser metatarsalgia at review and prospective-outcome level: the educational review of metatarsalgia differential diagnosis describes Morton's neuroma and plantar plate injury as the two main causes of lesser metatarsalgia (PMID 37230133), the anatomy and pathomechanism review describes the common plantar digital nerve compression producing characteristic forefoot pain (PMID 33168237), and the prospective observational outcomes study of 138 patients records Morton's neuroma as associated with chronic pain and disability with metatarsal-region pain scores as the primary outcome measure (PMID 33019802); the relationship is recorded as documented clinical-causation framing at review class only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: metatarsalgia is both the presenting symptom complex of Morton's neuroma and a distinct clinical syndrome with plantar plate injury, Freiberg disease, and inflammatory causes, so any individual metatarsalgia attribution requires ultrasound-confirmed nerve thickening with plantar-plate, bursal, and inflammatory exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Chronic compression of the common plantar digital nerve between metatarsal heads drives perineural fibrosis and neuropathic firing so plantar forefoot pain in the metatarsal region results, the nerve-entrapment route documented by the pathomechanism review and consistent with the metatarsalgia framing of the differential-diagnosis review, but whether this route produced any individual metatarsalgia presentation remains hypothesized until ultrasound and clinical records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at review plus prospective-outcome class only: the causation framing is from educational and imaging reviews rather than incidence cohorts, the prospective outcomes study measures pain severity rather than metatarsalgia incidence, and the catalog's published forefoot-identity windows (hallux-valgus, mallet-toes) carry their own metatarsalgia evidence which is not recycled here (ME-29).
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No located cohort quantifies metatarsalgia incidence attributable to Morton's neuroma; constitutive-proximity tension is recorded because forefoot pain is simultaneously the defining symptom of Morton's neuroma and the metatarsalgia syndrome; intermetatarsal bursitis is documented to mimic Morton's neuroma on clinical grounds (PMID 40677501); and plantar plate tears, Freiberg disease, and inflammatory arthritis are competing metatarsalgia causes.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: intermetatarsal bursitis (documented clinical mimic; the located ultrasound case, PMID 40677501)
plantar plate injury (the review's co-primary cause of lesser metatarsalgia)
Freiberg disease and metatarsal stress fracture
hallux valgus and lesser-toe deformity mechanics (the published sibling windows, not recycled per ME-29)

evidenceGaps: No located cohort quantifies metatarsalgia incidence attributable to Morton's neuroma; constitutive-proximity tension is recorded because forefoot pain is simultaneously the defining symptom of Morton's neuroma and the metatarsalgia syndrome; intermetatarsal bursitis is documented to mimic Morton's neuroma on clinical grounds (PMID 40677501); and plantar plate tears, Freiberg disease, and inflammatory arthritis are competing metatarsalgia causes.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on the clinical-causation-review precedent with the constitutive-proximity tension carried openly: the metatarsalgia differential review names Morton's neuroma and plantar plate injury as the two main causes of lesser metatarsalgia (PMID 37230133), the pathomechanism review documents common plantar digital nerve compression (PMID 33168237), and the 138-patient prospective outcomes study records chronic pain and disability (PMID 33019802); because forefoot pain is both the defining symptom of Morton's neuroma and the metatarsalgia syndrome and no cohort quantifies attributable incidence, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through ultrasound-confirmed nerve thickening with plantar-plate, bursal, and inflammatory exclusion.
